column3: hey; oh (to get attention or show surprise)
column5: Hey, you dropped your phone!
column6: 哎 is a light interjection used to get attention or show mild surprise.

column5: Oh dear, I forgot to bring my phone!
column6: 哎呀 shows surprise, worry or regret.

column5: Sigh, there is too much homework today.
column6: 唉 is read ài when it is a sigh. It is read āi when it answers someone ("yes?").

column3: to take good care of; to cherish
column5: We must take good care of the environment.

column4: 他走了以后，我才安下心来。
column5: After he left, I finally felt at ease.
column6: 安 is mostly used inside words: 安全, 安静, 安心, 平安.

column5: You must always fasten your seat belt when you drive.
column6: 系 is read jì here, "to fasten".

column5: My friend comforted me for a long time.
The workers are coming today to install the air conditioner.

column4: 房间里太暗了，我看不清楚。
column5: It is too dark in the room; I cannot see clearly.
Staying up late is not good for your health.
column6: 熬夜 is a verb plus object: 熬了一夜, 别熬夜.

column3: confidence (that something will work out); to seize
column5: I am very confident about this exam.
column6: 把握 is also a verb, "to seize" (把握机会).

column4: 我白跑了一趟，他不在家。
column5: I made a trip for nothing; he was not at home.
column6: 白 also means "white" (HSK 1). Used as an adverb, it means "in vain".

column3: midnight; the middle of the night
column5: The child cried in the middle of the night.
At dusk the sky is very red.
Your parcel has arrived.
column6: 包裹 is also a verb, "to wrap up".

column5: This price includes breakfast.
column6: 包含 is for what is part of something. 包括 lists the items.

column4: 我们一共有十个人，包括孩子。
column5: There are ten of us altogether, including the children.

column4: 这个礼物的包装很漂亮。
column5: The packaging of this gift is very beautiful.

column4: 这本书很薄，一天就能看完。
column5: This book is thin; you can finish it in one day.
column6: 薄 is for flat things like books, paper and clothes. 瘦 is for people and animals.

column4: 这个孩子是爸爸妈妈的宝。
column5: This child is the treasure of his parents.
column6: 宝 is mostly used inside words: 宝贝, 宝贵, 宝宝.

column3: to protect; to guarantee; to keep
column5: The phones in this shop come with a one-year warranty.
column6: 保 is mostly used inside words: 保护, 保证, 保险, 保持.

column5: There is a security guard at the gate of the neighbourhood.
column6: 保安 is a security guard: 小区保安 (a guard in a residential area).

column5: Mum often calls her daughter “darling”.
column6: 宝贝 is a loving name for a child or a partner, and also any treasured thing.

column5: Please keep quiet.

column4: 文件写好以后要记得保存。
column5: After you write a file, you need to remember to save it.
Time is the most precious thing.

column3: to keep; to reserve; to retain
column4: 这个座位给你保留到六点。
column5: This seat is reserved for you until six o'clock.
When you buy a car, you must buy insurance.
column6: 保险 is also an adjective, "safe, sure" (这样比较保险).

column4: 这种牛奶的保质期是一个星期。
column5: This kind of milk has a shelf life of one week.

column3: to report for duty; to register on arrival
column4: 新同学明天上午来学校报到。
column5: The new students come to the school tomorrow morning to register.
column6: 报到 is a verb plus object: 报了到.

column4: 报纸上有一篇关于这件事的报道。
column5: There is a report about this matter in the newspaper.
column6: 报道 is read bàodào, like 报到, but the characters and meanings differ.

column5: The manager tells me to write a report.

column4: 发现包不见了，他马上报警了。
column5: Finding that his bag was gone, he called the police at once.
column6: 报警 is a verb plus object: 报了警.

column4: 今天有暴雨，我们在家吧。
column5: There is a heavy rainstorm today, so let us stay at home.
He is always complaining that work is too tiring.

column3: behind; at the back; behind someone's back
column5: He is standing behind me.
column6: 背后 also means "in secret": 不要在背后说别人。

column4: 这张照片的背景是一座大山。
column5: The background of this photo is a big mountain.
It is cold now, so you need a thick quilt.
This is a famous local snack.
column6: 本地 is used before a noun: 本地人, 本地新闻.

column4: 她有很多本领，会唱歌，也会画画。
column5: She has many skills: she can sing and also draw.

column3: oneself; the person himself or herself
column5: This letter must be handed to the person himself.

column4: 问题的本质是时间不够。
column5: The essence of the problem is that there is not enough time.
We understand each other very well.
column6: 彼此 is also said as a polite answer to a compliment: 彼此彼此.

column5: The score is now two to one.

column4: 这个班男生和女生的比例是一比二。
column5: The ratio of boys to girls in this class is one to two.

column3: to compare (as a figure of speech); metaphor
column4: 人们常用河水来比喻时间。
column5: People often use a river as a metaphor for time.
column6: 比喻 is also a noun, "a metaphor".

column5: As long as you work hard, you will certainly gain something.
column6: 必 is formal and written. In speech people say 一定 or 必须.

column4: 他毕竟还是个孩子，别太生气。
column5: After all, he is still a child, so do not be too angry.

column4: 为了避免迟到，我提前出门。
column5: To avoid being late, I leave home early.

column4: 运动会的闭幕式在晚上举行。
column5: The closing ceremony of the sports meeting is held in the evening.

column4: 努力学习必然会有进步。
column5: Studying hard will inevitably lead to progress.
column6: 必然 is also a noun, "what is bound to happen".

column4: 对旅行来说，护照是必需的。
column5: For travel, a passport is essential.
column6: 必需 is read bìxū. 必须 is also read bìxū, but it is an adverb, "must".

column5: There is no need to be in such a hurry.
column6: 没有必要 means "there is no need".

column5: As soon as he got home, he went to sleep.
column6: 便 is the written form of 就. 便 is also read pián in 便宜.

column4: 飞机的时间有变动，请注意。
column5: The flight time has changed; please pay attention.
column6: 变动 is also a noun, "a change".

column5: Shopping here is very convenient.
column6: 便利 is a little more formal than 方便.

column4: 我常常在便利店买早饭。
column5: I often buy breakfast at the convenience store.

column4: 这篇文章的标题很有意思。
column5: The title of this article is very interesting.

column4: 这个标志的意思是不能抽烟。
column5: This sign means that smoking is not allowed.

column4: 我不知道怎么用汉语表达我的想法。
column5: I do not know how to express my ideas in Chinese.
The surface of the table is very clean.
column6: 表面 also means "on the outside": 表面上很高兴.

column4: 调查表明，大部分人喜欢这个办法。
column5: The survey shows that most people like this method.
His expression is very serious.

column4: 早饭我吃了一张饼和一个鸡蛋。
column5: For breakfast I had a pancake and an egg.
column6: 饼 is any flat round food. It takes the measure word 张 or 块.

column5: He is staying in a ward on the third floor.

column4: 医生说他的病情已经好转了。
column5: The doctor said his condition has already improved.

column4: 有问题请拨打这个电话。
column5: If you have a question, please call this number.
column6: 拨打 is used with phone numbers: 拨打电话, 拨打110.

column4: 孩子不小心打破了玻璃。
column5: The child accidentally broke the glass.
column6: 玻璃 is the material of windows and bottles. A drinking glass is 杯子.

column4: 这个博物馆星期一不开门。
column5: This museum is not open on Mondays.
The weather is unfavourable for the match.
Unfortunately he fell ill.
column6: 不幸 is also a noun, "misfortune".

column4: 这个病不要紧，吃点药就会好。
column5: This illness is not serious; you will get better after taking some medicine.
Do you have anything else to add?
He is extremely happy.
column6: 不得了 after 得 means "extremely": 好得不得了. On its own it means "terrible!": 不得了了！

column3: to not match; to not fit
column5: What you say does not match the facts.
He has many bad habits.
column6: 不良 is formal and is used before nouns: 不良习惯, 不良影响.
